propositions: When push non-fast-forward recovery encounters an untracked local file colliding with a file the merge wants to create, the merge aborts and recovery gives up without self-healing.
The same untracked-overwrite collision class that wedged reconverge (compaction leftovers like *-SNAPSHOT.json and *.retired) also wedges push_recovery's _recover_dirty_merge.
After quarantining named colliding untracked paths and retrying the merge once, the push recovery completes with both parents and restores tracked edits from stash without data loss.
Genuine conflicts and paths git does not name in the merge abort message preserve today's behavior (abort, restore stash, warn or strict-raise).
The stash commit object is restored exactly once on all exit paths (success, retry-failure, non-recoverable abort) so tracked edits are never lost.
